samples.summary: No test covers the new `readOnly` gate in YorkieStore (constructor presence seed, updateSelection, ensureAxisOrder)
samples.evidence: The delta adds three write suppressions in YorkieStore (constructor `activeTabId` seed at yorkie-store.ts:109, `updateSelection` at :651, `ensureAxisOrder` at :689). Every construction site in tests passes only two args: tests/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-axis-order.test.ts:60, tests/helpers/single-user-yorkie.ts:54, tests/helpers/two-user-yorkie.ts:47, tests/helpers/two-user-spreadsheet-yorkie.ts:103-104, tests/helpers/cross-sheet-yorkie.ts:101 — so `readOnly` is never true in any suite. Nothing asserts that a read-only mount produces zero doc.update()s (e.g. unchanged doc.getRoot().sheets[tab].rowOrder / no presence change / no local change pending) nor that a writable mount still seeds and publishes. If the gate regresses, a share-link viewer silently writes `rowOrder`/`colOrder` into the shared CRDT root and wedges their own sync — a data-affecting, user-visible failure with no test to catch it. Notably the same PR did add such a test elsewhere (tests/app/files/pdf-collab-provider.test.tsx:74 'seeds nothing on a read-only mount'), so the pattern exists and was not applied here.

samples.summary: No test covers the new `readOnly` presence gate in YorkieDocStore (publishResolvedLocalCursor / updateCursorPos)
samples.evidence: The delta adds `if (this.readOnly) return;` at yorkie-doc-store.ts:1263 (publishResolvedLocalCursor) and :3199 (updateCursorPos), plus the new constructor arg. All test constructions pass a single argument — tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:36 and ~30 other sites, tests/app/docs/editor-undo-selection.test.ts:102/167/262, tests/app/docs/merge-repro.test.ts:55, tests/helpers/two-user-docs-yorkie.ts:111/137 — so the readOnly branch is never executed by any suite. There is no assertion that a read-only store leaves `doc.getMyPresence().activeCursorPos`/`activeSelection` untouched after updateCursorPos, nor that a writable store still publishes. A regression here reintroduces the `rw` PushPull that wedges a viewer's sync, which is exactly the bug this change claims to fix.

samples.summary: The explicitly-claimed 'anchoring still runs while presence is suppressed' behavior in read-only mode is untested
samples.evidence: The new comment on the `readOnly` field and at updateCursorPos asserts the gate 'suppresses the presence write only, never the caret anchoring ... localCursorAnchor / localSelectionAnchor ... keep a viewer's caret and selection where they were across a peer's edit.' No test constructs a read-only YorkieDocStore at all (see tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:36 and all other single-arg constructions), so nothing exercises updateCursorPos -> resolveAnchoredLocalCursor on a read-only store after a remote change. If the early return were ever moved above the anchor assignment, a viewer's caret would jump on every peer edit and no suite would notice; the failure is contained to a viewer's caret position, hence minor.

verdict.reason: The three readOnly write suppressions exist in YorkieStore (yorkie-store.ts:109 constructor presence seed, :651 updateSelection, :689 ensureAxisOrder) and readOnly is a live, reachable prop at sheet-view.tsx:130/1012. I enumerated every YorkieStore reference repo-wide: the only test-side constructions are yorkie-axis-order.test.ts:60, tests/helpers/single-user-yorkie.ts:54, two-user-yorkie.ts:47, two-user-spreadsheet-yorkie.ts:103-104 and cross-sheet-yorkie.ts:101 — all two-arg, so readOnly is never true in any suite, and nothing asserts a read-only mount emits zero doc.update()s (nor that a writable mount still seeds/publishes). I also searched wider for an indirect counterexample and found none: no e2e/playwright sheet spec, no colocated src/app/spreadsheet test touching the store, no test rendering SheetView with readOnly (preview-surface.test.tsx:155 is only a source-string scan). Near-misses are different code paths, not this gate: frontend/src/types/worksheet.test.ts:11 covers sheetsInitialRootForRole('viewer') (attach-time initialRoot), packages/sheets/test/sheet/sheet.test.ts overrides ensureAxisOrder/updateSelection on MemStore to test engine coverage bounds, and packages/sheets/src/store/readonly.ts ReadOnlyStore serves query-result display. The analogous test does exist for the sibling surface (tests/app/files/pdf-collab-provider.test.tsx:74 'seeds nothing on a read-only mount'), showing the pattern was simply not applied here. Blocking under the test-adequacy rubric: a changed guard on a user-facing path (share-link viewer silently writing rowOrder/colOrder into the shared CRDT root and wedging sync) with no meaningful test — major.

A repo-wide grep for 'YorkieDocStore(' shows the flag is passed at exactly one site, the production one (docs-view.tsx:364); every test construction passes a single argument (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:36 plus ~30 inline reads, editor-undo-selection.test.ts:102/167/262, editor-step-selection-font-size-undo.test.ts:90, merge-repro.test.ts:55, tests/helpers/two-user-docs-yorkie.ts:111/137). All existing cursor-presence tests use a writable store and assert presence IS published (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:558-567, :885-890; yorkie-doc-store-concurrent.integration.ts:429-435), so they pass identically whether the gate works or is deleted. I searched wider: case-insensitive read-only/readonly across all frontend test files, 'viewer' across frontend tests, repo-wide readOnlyDocStore, and presence/cursor greps inside packages/docs/test/view/editor-read-only.test.ts (no presence assertions there, only resize-cursor styling); there is no e2e suite for docs. The only mock-based construction (src/app/documents/__tests__/apply-imported-content.test.ts:51/108) mocks the class away and asserts a single-arg call. No test executes the readOnly=true branch, so the guard is untested; its regression re-enables the 'rw' PushPull the auth webhook refuses a share-link viewer, wedging that viewer's sync on a real user path — major.
